prompt: Some people think that the increasing use of computers and mobile phones nowadays has unwanted effects on young people's reading and writing skills. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
essay:
The widespread use of computers and smartphones has raised concerns about their impact on young people's reading and writing abilities. Although excessive dependence on these devices can weaken independent literacy skills, I largely disagree that their increasing use is inherently harmful because they provide young people with greater access to information and opportunities to develop these skills.

One major benefit of digital devices is that they give students easy access to a vast amount of written material. Instead of relying solely on textbooks or spending considerable time searching for resources in libraries, young people can find academic articles, books and educational websites within seconds. Regular exposure to such material can improve their reading skills by introducing them to different writing styles, vocabulary and ideas. Moreover, computers make writing considerably more convenient because students can draft, edit and reorganise their work easily. For example, a student preparing an academic assignment can consult several reliable online sources and revise their work repeatedly before submitting it.

However, excessive reliance on technology can have negative consequences, particularly when young people use it as a substitute for independent thinking and writing. This problem has become more evident with the growing availability of artificial intelligence tools. Students can now generate essays and summaries within seconds, which may discourage them from developing their own ability to organise ideas and construct sentences. Similarly, spending excessive amounts of time consuming short online content may reduce the time young people devote to reading longer and more demanding texts. Therefore, the problem is not the technology itself but the way it is used.

In conclusion, I largely disagree that the growing use of computers and mobile phones necessarily harms young people's reading and writing abilities. While excessive dependence on digital technology and AI can weaken independent literacy skills, responsible use of these devices can provide valuable opportunities to read widely, access information and improve writing.
